question: What Are Grouped Products, and When Should I Use Them?
metaDescription: A collection of separate, independently purchasable products shown together on one page — useful for a curated set without forcing a bundled purchase.
shortAnswer: A grouped product presents several separate, individually existing products together on one page, each still independently purchasable (with its own quantity selector), rather than combining them into a single bundled item with one price. This differs from a variable product, since the individual items in a group are genuinely separate products (each could also be sold on its own elsewhere), not variations of one underlying product.

bodyHtml:
How Grouped Products Work

Creating a grouped product involves selecting a set of existing, already-created products to associate together, and the resulting page displays all of them in a table-like layout, each with its own quantity field, letting a customer choose exactly which items (and how many of each) to add to their cart from that one page — genuinely different from a bundle where the whole set is purchased as a single line item.

Good Use Cases

  • A curated collection (a set of related accessories, a themed product line) where customers benefit from seeing everything together, but should still choose individually which items they actually want.
  • A product family where each variant genuinely functions as its own standalone product elsewhere in the catalog too, rather than existing only as part of the group.
  • Not the right choice for a genuine bundle-at-a-discount offer, since grouped products don't apply special combined pricing — a dedicated bundle/kit plugin is the correct tool for that specific need instead.
  • Not the right choice for size/color-style variation, which is what variable products (covered elsewhere) are specifically built for.

Setting Up a Grouped Product

  1. Create the individual products first, since a grouped product references existing product listings.
  2. Create the grouped product and associate the relevant existing products with it.
  3. Confirm this is the right tool for the actual goal — a curated collection versus a genuine discounted bundle need different WooCommerce approaches.
